content:
For a draft lean4 PR, what's the new way to get (the equivalent of) a lean pr testing branch for mathlib which allows me to bench mathlib and add commits fixing it up if necessary?

I was recently clued into lean4#15098 from 2 days ago, so I'm wondering both (1) if I just so happened to run a core experiment at a bad time :) (2) what the future (or current?) workflow looks like :)

Yes, the mechanism is fairly new. One needs to add the downstream label to one's PR. After that (or perhaps after pushing the next commit), the CI should link a PR in https://github.com/leanprover/downstream-lean4, and there one can call !bench mathlib. I'm not sure about how the permissions for the new mechanism look like, though...
Ah, okay! I've tried commenting downstream on my PR, but that doesn't seem to have attached the downstream label; should I be doing something different?
Which one is your PR?
That'd be lean4#15138 :)
Are there base requirements? I tried to rebase onto nightly-with-mathlib before I was aware of this; should I be doing something else now?
Oh, yes, there are! You need to rebase or merge downstream-green. (Yes, merging works now, too.)
Clarification: I meant that you need to add the label downstream so that CI picks it up, not a comment.
I can't add a label, unfortunately, permission-wise :upside_down:
(I was hoping that comments would be turned into labels as some other comments are)
(I think the behavior I was hoping for is managed in .github/workflows/labels-from-comments.yml?)

Hmm, I'm not familiar with how the permissions work; I believe the issue is that downstream-lean4 isn't in leanprover-community anymore. Is there already a mechanism how Mathlib contributors can use downstream if they need to experiment with the toolchain, @Joscha Mennicken? I wonder whether a separate downstream-lean4 repo inside leanprover-community could help, but I'm out of my depth here, also which mechanism is good security-wise.
I added the label to your PR, let's see whether this already helps for now.

Thanks! :) Yeah, I suppose there are two issues: one, only users with triage/write access for the lean4 repo can manage labels on core PRs in the first place (unless labels-from-comments.yml were to allow a comment to add the label); and then, permission would also (presumably?) be needed to make adaptations in the resulting PR in downstream-lean4.

We were planning on adding additional contributors to downstream-lean4 as necessary (@Thomas Murrills invite sent), and I'll have a look at how to label PRs downstream or downstream-force without additional permissions tomorrow.

Paul Reichert said:

Oh, yes, there are! You need to rebase or merge downstream-green. (Yes, merging works now, too.)

More specifically, the merge base needs to be downstream-green, which is why rebasing may be necessary if you branched off of a more recent commit. The bot will warn you if your PR doesn't fulfill this criterion.

Paul Reichert said:

One needs to add the downstream label to one's PR. After that (or perhaps after pushing the next commit), […]

It should not be necessary to push another commit. If it is, that's a bug, please tell me about it :)

I will update https://github.com/leanprover-community/leanprover-community.github.io/blob/lean4/templates/contribute/tags_and_branches.md with info on downstream-lean4 soon as well; at the moment it contains outdated information on the old system. (If there's other places you'd have expected information on this workflow, please let me know.)

Joscha Mennicken said:

It should not be necessary to push another commit. If it is, that's a bug, please tell me about it :)

I do believe I recently tried, and it worked well, so no reason to believe pushing a commit is necessary. :+1:

lean4#15155 should hopefully let anyone with write access to downstream-lean4 label a lean4 PR with downstream/downstream-force by commenting. @Thomas Murrills, could you maybe try labeling one of your existing lean PRs to test whether it works as intended?

@Joscha Mennicken Thanks! I’ve tried it on lean4#15150 which is based on downstream-green, but didn’t get a label. Is the commit adding the workflow just too recent? (Does a PR use master’s workflows or its own? :thinking:)

Ah, I see it worked for you! :D

For what it’s worth I believe I accepted the invitation to downstream-lean4 yesterday.

When I commented, the label was added, but your comment doesn't seem to show up in https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/actions/workflows/labels-from-comments.yml. I suspect it's some sort of github actions permission issue?
Ah, your comment was a PR review, not a plain comment, but the action in its current form only responds to plain (issue) comments. I've removed the label and you can try again if you want.
Aha, great, it works! :) (Sorry about that, I have no idea why GitHub turned my original comment into a review :sweat_smile:)
It's still somewhat broken though, apparently the adaptation PR CI that ran thought the PR didn't have the downstream label.
Should be fixed now, I think.
Everything appears to be working now. Thanks for helping me test, @Thomas Murrills :D
Happy to help, ty for making it work!! :smile:
